newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Cofinec GDRs edge up after 9-month results.
newsitem.headline: Cofinec GDRs edge up after 9-month results.

text.p: French-registered packaging company Cofinec rose slightly on the Budapest Stock Exchange after the release of its January-September earnings report.
Cofinec Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) opened unchanged from Thursday's close of 4,100 forints and later put on minor gains to as high as 4,150. At 1159 GMT the shares traded at 4,100 forints.
The company, the first foreign issue on the Budapest bourse, published its nine-month results this morning. @

The group's IAS consolidated January-September net sales slipped to 492.8 million French francs from 497.5 million francs in the same period of last year, although showed some rebound in September alone.
"Sales in September increased as customer activity accelerated in Hungary, following seasonally slow sales in July and August," the company said in its report.
The company's net result showed a loss of 19.2 million francs against 13.0 million in profit in the same period of last year. @
"Net loss of 19.2 million French francs for the first nine months were in line with revised expectations as indicated in the company's announcement of September 9, 1996," it said.
The company saw several reasons behind the losses.

"Lower results are mainly due to economic slowdown in Hungary which affected customer orders at Petofi (its printing house unit), especially between May and August and extensive trial order production runs at Cofinec Polska resulting in higher costs and a revenue shortfall."
Cofinec said it performed better on its export markets. @
"Export marketing showes success as the ratio of exports to total sales has increased to over 10 percent, helped by new sales initiatives in the promising Russian and Ukrainian markets."
The company said it was expecting a more favourable environment for 1997.
"Customer demand in Hungary is improving and prospects for the flexible packaging business in Poland are particularly strong."
